phases.name: Pin idempotence and the path guard

steps.name: Pin build idempotence and the --merge/--out path guard
criteria: Running build --out <t> --merge <t> twice over the same cache leaves the tracker's content unchanged by the second run: every cell value, type and number format on every tab after run 2 equals run 1, including human-owned values, a date-formatted cell, an unknown column and a second tab.
The second run reports 0 cell changes.
The second run does not add rows or columns.

build --merge <a> --out <b> with different paths refuses with a non-zero exit, names both flags in its message, and leaves <a> byte-identical and <b> byte-identical if it existed or absent if it did not.
Both scenarios are shown to be non-vacuous: each fails against a deliberately wrong implementation, and the failure is shown rather than claimed.
Suite: 136 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped rises by exactly the scenarios added, all passing.
steps.scenario_name: a repeated build is a no-op; merge and out must name the same tracker
steps.implementation_notes: Captures two behaviours that were only hand-checked (idempotence) or implemented without a test (the merge/out refusal) — user decision 2026-09-17. Both land AFTER target-sheet-apply 01-02 implements them, so they will be GREEN on arrival; non-vacuity must be demonstrated with adversaries: for idempotence, an apply that appends instead of updating, or that writes a run-varying value such as appliedAt into a cell; for the path guard, a build that applies to --out while ignoring --merge. Compare cell CONTENT across runs, not file digests: xlsx is a zip and may carry write timestamps, so byte-identity across runs is not the property — measure whether SheetJS output is deterministic before choosing, and use the stronger assertion only if it genuinely holds.
